question: When equal search on two plausible moves changes which is preferable, does a player anticipate the revision? Distinguish this from general agreement with a strong engine, willingness to depart from its policy, and which positions each player faces. Derive menus before reading the actual move. Do not infer human mental search depth.
prior: R1 family A and H already tried opening/pattern books. M23/M25 compared general policy/search agreement, lead and win-rate losses including search features over no-search; M29 measured returning an opponent's gift. Earlier alternative_choice_20261118 tested straight escapes versus local rescues. Here the same pre-action top-two legal policy options on unrestricted boards receive paired, equal-budget child evaluations and an explicit raw-versus-searched revision contrast.
data: Use all verified R1 fold 1-4 historical validation games aligned exactly to SQ4 (5/10/20 games). From separate raw games of evaluation-fold owners select up to four per owner by the smallest deterministic, label-blind digest per owner; remove raw games in any historical question and duplicate raw SGFs. These fresh games are a replication of the behavioral contrasts on new games of participating players; they have no SQ4 question predictions. Use no fold 0, official questions or leaderboard. Historical evaluation players have appeared in earlier project research.
sampling: On each target side sample one pre-action turn by digest within each of twelve successive windows of 16 plies starting at ply 20 (zero based). Index offsets without seeing the move, phase coverage, length beyond that turn, or grade. No replacement of a missing scheduled turn. Replay exact handicap and color, same Japanese rules and komi as M25.
menu: With the strong external KataGo kata1-b18c384nbt-s9996604416-d4316597426 v1.18.2 binary, fixed symmetry, take the two highest entries in the pre-search legal policy on the full board. Denote first A, second B, lower index on exact ties. Neither can be pass. Require pB >= .05, pA/pB <=4, pA+pB>=.30. Record all eligible opportunities including actual outside choices. Audit legality, row order and viewpoint. At each chosen state append A or B to exactly the same history and evaluate each child with 24 visits. For a prespecified 1/32 hash sample also run 128 visits per child. Store root.rawLead for the child, root.scoreLead after search and currentPlayer. Mover-view d0 and d24 are lead of B minus lead of A (opponent-view lead of A minus B). Operational strong reversal: signs opposite and both magnitudes >=0.5 points. Define the same rule for d128 as the numerical audit. Budgets are per candidate.
methods: For positions in which the player picks A or B use Bernoulli likelihood of B. Grade-independent covariates: intercept, log(pB/pA), joint policy mass, phase, absolute pre-move lead, clipped d0, signed searched winner, incremental clipped d24 minus clipped d0, signed strong-reversal flag. The marginal grade model allows deviations for intercept, log policy odds, raw child difference and signed searched winner. Thus ordinary preference and general agreement with the searched winner are already allowed to vary by grade. The depth model additionally allows grade-specific coefficients for incremental value revision and signed strong-reversal. Fit weighted mean log loss with each observed training player equally weighted within grade and grades equally weighted, ridge .002 on shared slopes and .01 times mean of per-grade squared deviations. Per-question evidence is the sum of grade-specific response log likelihoods divided by sqrt(max(K,1)); outside moves remain recorded but do not enter the binary likelihood.
rank_head: Fit ranks and action models only on folds 1/2. On player-out inner predictions (fold 1 predicts 2, fold 2 predicts 1), calibrate nonnegative temperatures on balanced question NLL in [0,2], first for marginal log evidence over frozen SQ4, then for full-minus-marginal evidence on top. Freeze both and fit response coefficients on the union for evaluation folds 3/4. The ordinary common model reproduces SQ4. Negative control shuffles the two depth-specific covariates together on unique positions inside fold, phase, raw prior-odds group, raw value-direction group, and searched winner, with seed 20261118, keeping the rest fixed. Reuse original SQ4 guard and competition metric. Test all ten grades, with prespecified detailed 1D/2D and 3D/4D comparisons.
decision: Call a rank candidate only if full minus SQ4 >=0.001 with both held-out folds positive, and paired player 95% lower bounds above zero vs both SQ4 and marginal. Report counts of changed/better/worse questions, NLL, scores by size, raw untempered sensitivity as diagnostic if the fitted coefficient is zero, grade-controlled matched behavior without shrinkage, and uncertainty from player-stratified resampling. Do not tune on evaluation. Examine opposing signs on strong reversals, coverage per 5-game question, and split-half stability. For the fresh games report held-out behavioral effects, not a competition score.
